evals.prompt: I run marketing at a small literary publisher. Our monthly email newsletter 'The Shelf' — a staff book pick, a list of new releases, and a short author interview — has slipped from 31% to 22% open rate over the past year and clicks are flat. Use SCAMPER to come up with ideas to make it fresh again, and tell me which ones to try first.
evals.expected_output: Full SCAMPER session: framed goal, attributes, ideas under all 7 letters with bold ideas, scored shortlist, prioritized next steps with tests.
expectations: Opens with a SCAMPER map table listing at least 2 areas with parts/limits and letters, plus an assumptions line
Ends with a 'What changed' table mapping original parts to new versions with letters, and a recommendation
Presents 3 named variations (A/B/C) as drafted concepts (concept cards or draft copy), not only idea lists
M ideas include at least one Magnify and one Minify
Each recommendation has a riskiest assumption and a cheapest test
Addresses the open-rate problem specifically (subject line / sender / preview / timing)
Backlog of undrafted ideas is 8 items or fewer

evals.prompt: here's the back-cover blurb for a debut psychological thriller ... give me 3 rewritten options.
evals.expected_output: Three finished rewritten blurbs, each labelled with the SCAMPER operator(s) behind it, cliches removed, a recommendation.
expectations: Opens with a SCAMPER map table listing at least 2 areas with parts/limits and letters, plus an assumptions line
Ends with a 'What changed' table mapping original parts to new versions with letters, and a recommendation
Shows the original blurb, then three complete rewritten blurbs ready to use
Each rewrite is labelled with a name and the SCAMPER letters behind it
None of the rewrites use 'better left buried', 'race against time', or 'put it down'
Invented plot specifics are flagged as placeholders

evals.prompt: Our online bookstore checkout is 5 steps: cart → create account → shipping address → payment → review & confirm. Mobile abandonment is around 70%. What could we eliminate, and what could we reverse or rearrange? Give me concrete changes.
evals.expected_output: Deep Eliminate and Reverse/Rearrange pass on checkout steps, concrete changes, prioritized, with tests and UX caveats.
expectations: Opens with a SCAMPER map table listing at least 2 areas with parts/limits and letters, plus an assumptions line
Ends with a 'What changed' table mapping original parts to new versions with letters, and a recommendation
Focuses on Eliminate and Reverse/Rearrange rather than a full 7-letter session
Proposes guest checkout / account after purchase
Shows at least one variation as a before -> after flow of checkout steps
Recommends testing/measuring the changes

evals.prompt: repurpose this infographic design with this topic "How To Give Feedback Without Overexplaining"
evals.expected_output: Slot inventory/map with layout and content areas, three variations (faithful / re-meant / remixed) rendered as design artboards or an HTML side-by-side file, What changed table by slot, no source branding.

evals.prompt: We're launching Mira Okafor's debut novel 'The Salt Orchard' next month. Our landing page hero is: big cover image on the left, headline 'A Sweeping Family Saga', subhead 'The debut everyone is talking about', and a 'Buy Now' button. Give me three better hero section variations.
evals.expected_output: Map (layout + copy + CTA areas), three hero variations rendered visually (artboards or HTML side by side) with real copy, What changed table, recommendation.
expectations: Opens with a SCAMPER map table listing at least 2 areas with parts/limits and letters, plus an assumptions line
Ends with a 'What changed' table mapping original parts to new versions with letters, and a recommendation
Produces visual drafts of 3 hero sections (artboards or one HTML file), not only text
Each variation has real headline, subhead and CTA copy within typical limits (headline <= 10 words, CTA 2-4 words)
At least one variation changes the CTA beyond 'Buy Now' (e.g. preview, first chapter, preorder bonus)
Unknown facts (quotes, awards, dates) are placeholders, not invented
